idiom_name: KafkaJS eachBatch / amqplib headers plus a Map of per-sequence buffers
implementation_notes: Node has no messaging in the standard library, so the realization is a header convention plus a Map of buffers: KafkaJS orders records inside a partition and its eachBatch handler feeds a whole partition batch (resolveOffset and heartbeat let you commit only after a group is out), while amqplib attaches the three fields as AMQP header fields on channel.publish. Position and size travel in the headers, ordering comes from the partition or the queue, and the release logic remains application code.
pitfalls: eachBatch handlers may run concurrently for different partitions (partitionsConsumedConcurrently), so the group Map must be shared safely and a group must never span partitions.
AMQP header values are typed field-table entries: publishing pos or size as strings makes the position arithmetic silently misbehave.
In-memory buffers die with the process; without a durable group store a restart loses every partial group.
